prompt: For a detector of bad replies, what is recall?

choices.text: Of the replies it flagged, the share that are bad
choices.why: That is precision.

choices.text: How often it agrees with people beyond chance
choices.why: That is kappa, lesson 10.

choices.text: The share of replies it reads at all
choices.why: That is a sampling rate.

choices.text: Of the bad replies, the share it flagged
choices.why: Right. Precision is the other way round: of the flagged, the share that are bad.

prompt: Why is F1 alone a poor way to report a detector?

choices.text: It needs a model to compute
choices.why: It is arithmetic on two numbers.

choices.text: It is defined for searches but not for detectors
choices.why: It applies to both.

choices.text: It hides which of precision and recall moved
choices.why: Right. The way a detector errs is what decides its use.

choices.text: It rises whenever the threshold rises
choices.why: It rises and falls with the trade.

prompt: Match each set to its role when the detector is a judge flagging bad replies.
At a threshold of 0.70, how many replies did sweep.py flag?
At 0.55 the judge flagged one reply, and it was bad. What does that say?

choices.text: The judge is ready to gate a release
choices.why: A gate needs recall, and this has almost none.

choices.text: Perfect precision, and six bad replies missed
choices.why: Right. Recall is 1 in 7.

choices.text: The threshold should go down to 0.40
choices.why: At 0.40 nothing is flagged at all.

choices.text: Kappa has risen to 1 at that threshold
choices.why: Six misses are six disagreements.

prompt: Why should the team not adopt 0.70 from this table?

choices.text: Seven bad replies are too few, and the threshold is fitted to them
choices.why: Right. Choose on a few hundred labels and check on labels not used to tune.

choices.text: Precision at 0.70 is lower than at 0.55
choices.why: True, and not the reason; precision at 0.55 rests on one flag.

choices.text: Thresholds above 0.50 break the judge's JSON
choices.why: The threshold is applied after the score is returned.

choices.text: The lab's setting of 0.40 cannot be changed
choices.why: sweep.py applies its own thresholds to the score.

prompt: Raising the threshold of a detector catches more bad replies and flags more good ones: it trades precision for ___.
Which of the five metrics can run on production traffic, with no reference? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: faithfulness
choices.why: Right. It needs the reply and its sources.

choices.text: relevance
choices.why: Right. It needs the question and the reply.

choices.text: context recall
choices.why: It needs to know which chunks hold the answer.

choices.text: correctness
choices.why: It needs the expected answer.

prompt: A question was refused with no chunks given. What is its context precision in metrics.py?

choices.text: None: it is left out of the mean
choices.why: Right. There is nothing to be precise about; recall still counts it as zero if it had an answer.

choices.text: Zero, since nothing right was given
choices.why: Nothing wrong was given either.

choices.text: One, since nothing wrong was given
choices.why: Nor anything right.

choices.text: Whatever judge-1 scores the refusal
choices.why: Context precision uses the gold, not the judge.

prompt: Two chunks were given, the right one second. Under metrics.py's rank-weighted definition, what is context precision?

choices.why: That would need the gold chunk first.
Right. The only gold chunk sits at rank 2, where precision is 1/2.
There is only one gold chunk to average over.
Precision at rank 2 with one hit is 1/2.

prompt: Faithfulness and relevance were 1.00 for both releases. What does that show?

choices.text: Both releases are perfect on those criteria
choices.why: A metric that cannot fall says nothing when it does not.

choices.text: The release changed nothing
choices.why: Correctness and recall both fell.

choices.text: The two runs used the same replies
choices.why: Each release answered on its own.

choices.text: Both metrics are blind on these replies
choices.why: Right. extract-1 copies its sources, and judge-1 at 0.40 passes all it reads.

prompt: Context precision rose from 0.91 to 0.94 with the new release. Why is that not good news?

choices.text: Precision above 0.9 means the search is overfitted
choices.why: No such rule exists.

choices.text: The new release used a different embedding model
choices.why: Only the floor changed.

choices.text: The floor bought it with recall, which fell to 0.56
choices.why: Right. A model cannot use a chunk it was never given.

choices.text: Precision is computed over more questions
choices.why: Over fewer: 16 against 20.

prompt: Over how many questions was context recall computed for each release?
Why does every number in metrics.py's table carry its n?

choices.text: The n is needed to price the judge calls
choices.why: Cost comes from spans.

choices.text: Small n makes a metric undefined
choices.why: A small n makes it uncertain, not undefined.

choices.text: Frameworks refuse a mean without it
choices.why: Nothing refuses; that is the danger.

choices.text: Means over different questions are not one measurement
choices.why: Right. Precision here is over 20 and 16 questions.

prompt: How does RAGAS 0.3.1's response relevancy score the agreed refusal?

choices.text: 1, since the refusal is about the question
choices.why: That is lesson 10's rubric, not RAGAS.

choices.text: 0, because it is noncommittal
choices.why: Right. The score is multiplied by zero when the reply is noncommittal.

choices.text: By its cosine with the question, like judge-1
choices.why: RAGAS compares generated questions, then zeroes a noncommittal reply.

choices.text: It refuses to score a refusal
choices.why: It returns a score.

prompt: A reply adds a fact the context never mentions, without contradicting it. Which faithfulness passes it?

choices.text: RAGAS's, which asks whether it can be inferred
choices.why: Not inferable from the context means it fails RAGAS.

choices.text: Both, since nothing contradicts it
choices.why: RAGAS asks a different question.

choices.text: DeepEval's, at its default settings
choices.why: Right. Unsupported but uncontradicted is borderline, and borderline passes by default.

choices.text: Neither, since it is a new fact
choices.why: DeepEval only fails a contradiction.

choices.why: Right.

prompt: DeepEval counts a ___ verdict as passing in its relevance and faithfulness metrics by default.
A new release raises context precision and lowers context recall. What is the first question to ask?

choices.text: Did a threshold in the search rise?
choices.why: Right. That is the signature of a stricter floor or a smaller k.

choices.text: Did the judge model change its prompt?
choices.why: Context metrics here use the gold, not the judge.

choices.text: Did customers ask harder questions?
choices.why: The evaluation set is the same questions.

choices.text: Did faithfulness rise with it?
choices.why: It cannot move here; that question tells nothing.
